title: Checking an Ethernet Connection
overview: A wired Ethernet connection depends on a secure physical connection between the computer and the network device. A loose, damaged, or disconnected cable can prevent the computer from reaching the network.
checklist: Confirm the Ethernet cable is firmly connected to the computer.
Confirm the other end is connected to the router, switch, wall jack, or docking station.
Look for link or activity lights near the Ethernet port.
Inspect the cable and connector for visible damage.
Test with a known-good Ethernet cable when one is available.
common_indicators: No link or activity lights near the Ethernet port.
The connector feels loose or does not click into place.
Windows reports that the network cable is unplugged.
The connection works after reseating or replacing the cable.

quiz.question: What should you try when an Ethernet cable appears connected but there are no link lights?
answers: Reseat the cable or test a known-good cable
quiz.correct_answer: Reseat the cable or test a known-good cable
